statement: Adding a genuinely new rule `language` value to `rules/rules.json` (here: "iac", for the first non-{rust,typescript,python,common} language family) is safe on the Rust side (workspace build/test all green, other langs' count-parity completeness tests filter by their own `language` string so they are unaffected) but breaks the legacy pre-Rust `.mjs` enforcer's schema validator, which hardcodes `languages: ReadonlyArray<"rust"|"typescript"|"python"|"common">` (and a matching closed `family` enum) in src/rule-metadata.mjs / src/check-metadata.mjs. Running ocentra_enforcer_check (any check) scoped to files under the new crate throws "rule registry schema validation failed ... Expected 'rust'|'typescript'|'python'|'common', actual 'iac'" — a hard MCP-tool failure, not a lint finding.
why: The workpack's dogfood step ("run ocentra_enforcer_check on your files") assumes the check tool itself is language-agnostic w.r.t. rules.json's schema; it is not, because the MCP server currently still runs the legacy .mjs implementation, which was never updated for a new rule-family language. This is a cross-cutting fix outside crates/enforcer-lang-iac/**'s owns:, so it cannot be folded into this workpack without violating scope.
howToApply: Any future lane introducing a brand-new rule `language` (not rust/typescript/python/common) to rules/rules.json MUST expect ocentra_enforcer_check to hard-fail with a schema validation TypeError until src/rule-metadata.mjs and src/check-metadata.mjs's language/family enums are updated to match. Do not treat that MCP-tool error as a sign your own crate is broken (cargo test/clippy/fmt can all be green while this happens) — spawn/verify a background task against the legacy schema instead of trying to fix it inline (out of scope for a lang-crate workpack).

evidence.ref: ocentra_enforcer_check check=secrets and check=placeholder-implementation scoped to crates/enforcer-lang-iac: both threw 'rule registry schema validation failed ... ["languages"] ... Expected "rust"|"typescript"|"python"|"common", actual "iac"' after adding IAC-1.1..1.8 (language:"iac") to rules/rules.json

statement: enforcer-lang-ts's single `TriggerKind` (forbidden-substring-present) model does not cover the dominant IaC violation shape: "a resource type X is present but a REQUIRED companion key/block Y is absent anywhere in the file" (missing S3 encryption config, missing provider version pin, missing backend encrypt flag, missing CFN PublicAccessBlockConfiguration). Extended the shared `RuleSpec`/`SpecValidator` pattern with a second `TriggerKind::RequiredAbsent{scope_needle, required_needle}` variant: fires once per file (not per line) when `scope_needle` is found anywhere and `required_needle` is NOT found anywhere, anchored at the scope line; a file with no `scope_needle` occurrence is simply not-applicable (no finding), not a pass.
why: Config-shape/IaC rules are structurally presence/absence-of-companion-config checks, not forbidden-token checks — reusing enforcer-lang-ts's spec.rs verbatim would have required either faking a forbidden needle for "missing encryption" (impossible, there is no token for absence) or writing 5 bespoke hand-rolled validators, defeating the whole point of the data-driven RuleSpec table that makes count-parity completeness tests mechanical.
howToApply: Any future IaC-adjacent or config-shape rule family (arc-12 enforcer-lang-k8s, or a future enforcer-lang-security IaC slice) should reuse this two-TriggerKind RuleSpec shape (ForbiddenPresent + RequiredAbsent) rather than re-deriving it from scratch; RequiredAbsent's `scope_needle` acts as the applicability gate so the rule stays silent on files the rule doesn't apply to instead of false-firing on every file lacking the required key.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-lang-iac/src/rules/spec.rs TriggerKind::RequiredAbsent + crates/enforcer-lang-iac/src/rules/terraform.rs IAC-1.1/1.6/1.7 and cloudformation.rs IAC-1.4 all use it; run_fixture_parity passes fail/pass pairs for all 8 rules (12 unit + 1 completeness test, cargo test -p enforcer-lang-iac all green)
